items.followUp: What adaptations of villi help them absorb digested food efficiently?

rubric.why: Identifies villi and describes where they are found.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing villi as finger-like projections of the inner lining of the small intestine.

rubric.why: States how villi help absorb digested food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that villi increase the surface area for absorption of digested food or nutrients.

modelAnswer: Villi are tiny, finger-like projections of the inner lining of the small intestine.
They increase the surface area for absorption of digested food into the blood and lymph.

items.followUp: Describe the population level of biological organization and give an example.

rubric.why: Identifies what an individual is at this level of biological organization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining an individual as one living organism.

rubric.why: Explains that individuals may differ in their number of cells, with an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that an individual may be unicellular or multicellular and giving a suitable example.

rubric.why: Describes activities carried out by an individual organism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming essential life activities of an individual.

rubric.why: Provides an example of an individual organism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a valid example of one organism.

modelAnswer: An individual organism is a single living thing and represents the individual level of biological organization.
It may consist of one cell, as in Amoeba, or many cells, as in a human or a plant.
An individual carries out essential activities of life, such as nutrition, respiration, growth and reproduction.
Examples include one Amoeba, one human being or one plant.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and function of mitochondria, and draw a labelled diagram.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing lysosomes as small sacs bound by a single membrane.
Award 1 mark for stating that lysosomes contain digestive or hydrolytic enzymes.

rubric.why: States the role of lysosomal enzymes in digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that lysosomes digest foreign material, cellular waste or worn-out cell parts.

rubric.why: Assesses the requested labelled diagram, including a recognisable sketch and its labels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a lysosome sketch represented by a roughly 4 cm circle, and 1 mark for correctly labelling the single membrane and digestive enzymes.

modelAnswer: Lysosomes are small sacs in the cytoplasm, each bound by a single membrane.
These enzymes digest foreign material, cellular waste and worn-out cell parts.
Lysosomes are sometimes called suicidal bags of the cell because their enzymes can digest the cell if released.

Diagram: Draw a circle about 4 cm in diameter to represent a lysosome; draw a second, close concentric circle for its membrane; label the boundary “single membrane” and the inside “digestive enzymes.”

items.followUp: Compare Kingdom Fungi and Kingdom Animalia by describing their main characteristics.

rubric.why: States the defining cellular organization of Monera.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that monerans are prokaryotic and lack a true nucleus.

rubric.why: Describes the usual organization of monerans and gives an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Monera as generally unicellular and/or giving bacteria as an example.

rubric.why: Describes the cellular organization of plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that plants are multicellular eukaryotes with a true nucleus.

rubric.why: States characteristic plant structures and their role in nutrition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning cellulose cell walls and chloroplasts, and explaining that plants make food by photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: Kingdom Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms; their cells lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
Monerans are generally unicellular; bacteria are examples.
Kingdom Plantae consists of multicellular eukaryotic organisms with a true nucleus.
Plant cells usually have cellulose cell walls and chloroplasts containing chlorophyll.
Most plants make their own food by photosynthesis and store it mainly as starch.
